dialogue.conversations: You want to talk? Alright. What's on your mind?
dialogue.conversations/1: Sure, we can talk. What about?
dialogue.conversations/2: I'm listening. What do you want to know?
dialogue.conversations.cat.chitchat.food: What's good to eat around here?
dialogue.conversations.cat.profession.wo: Do you actually like your work?
dialogue.conversations.cat.village: The village, hm? What do you want to know?
dialogue.conversations.cat.village.peopl: What do you make of your neighbors?
dialogue.conversations.cat.events: News travels fast around here. What about it?
dialogue.conversations.cat.personal: Getting personal, are we? Go on, then.
dialogue.conversations.cat.personal.feel: How do you really feel about me?
dialogue.conversations.cat.relationships: That's close to my heart. What is it?
dialogue.conversations.work: Do you actually like your work?
dialogue.conversations.feelings: How do you really feel about me?
dialogue.conversations.checkin.good: Honestly? Pretty good. The bread turned out right and nobody's yelled at me yet.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.good/1: Better now that someone actually asked. Most folks just want directions.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.good/2: Can't complain. Slept through the night, and the roof only leaks in one spot now.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.rough: You want the honest answer? It's been a heavy few days. Thanks for asking, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.rough/1: Not my best morning. But you asking helps more than you'd think.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.again: You asked me that this morning, %1$s. Still the same answer.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.again/1: Twice in one day? Either you care a lot or you forgot you asked.
dialogue.conversations.day.good: Good one, actually. The well water was cold and the queue at the smith was short.
dialogue.conversations.day.good/1: It's the kind of day where the chickens behave. I'll take it.
dialogue.conversations.day.good/2: Sun's out, boots are dry. That's a win around here.
dialogue.conversations.day.rough: Long. My back aches and the cat knocked the stew off the table.
dialogue.conversations.day.rough/1: One of those days where the door sticks and everything else follows its lead.
dialogue.conversations.day.working: Busy hands today. Ask me again when I've put this down.
dialogue.conversations.day.working/1: In the middle of it, as you can see. But it's honest work.
dialogue.conversations.day.again: Same day it was an hour ago, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.day.again/1: Still going. Days don't change that fast around here.
dialogue.conversations.work.like: I do, most days. There's a rhythm to it. You stop noticing the blisters.
dialogue.conversations.work.like/1: It's mine, you know? Nobody tells me how to run my own bench.
dialogue.conversations.work.like/2: Ask me at dawn and I'll grumble. Ask me when it's done and I'm proud of it.
dialogue.conversations.work.hate: Between us? Some mornings I stare at the ceiling and think about just... walking.
dialogue.conversations.work.hate/1: It pays for bread. That's the nicest thing I can say about it.
dialogue.conversations.work.again: We covered my work already. It hasn't gotten more interesting since.
dialogue.conversations.village.home: %2$s? It's home. The bell's cracked and the gossip's fast, but it's home.
dialogue.conversations.village.home/1: I know every fence post in %2$s. Some days that's comfort, some days it's a cage.
dialogue.conversations.village.none: I don't really have a place. I go where the road goes.
dialogue.conversations.village.none/1: No village claims me right now. It's quieter that way, mostly lonelier.
dialogue.conversations.village.again: Still the same village, %1$s. The fences haven't moved.
dialogue.conversations.life.first: My life? Nobody's asked me that before. Give me a second... it's a long story with a lot of turnips in it.
dialogue.conversations.life.first/1: Where do I even start? Born here, scraped knees here, buried my father behind the chapel. Still here.
dialogue.conversations.life.first/2: It's been quiet mostly. One flood, one bad winter, one summer I still think about.
dialogue.conversations.life.revisit: You asked me about my life once. I've been thinking about what I left out.
dialogue.conversations.life.revisit/1: Remember when you asked about my life? I remembered the good parts after you left.
dialogue.conversations.life.again: I just told you my whole story. Let it breathe a little.
dialogue.conversations.dreams.first: Don't laugh. I want to see the ocean once. Just once. Smell the salt.
dialogue.conversations.dreams.first/1: I dream about a bigger garden. And once, flying. The garden feels more likely.
dialogue.conversations.dreams.first/2: Someday I want to build something that outlasts me. A bridge, maybe. Or a family.
dialogue.conversations.dreams.revisit: Still dreaming about what I told you. It hasn't gotten smaller.
dialogue.conversations.dreams.again: You know my dream already. Saying it twice won't make it come faster.
You think so? Then maybe I'll actually do it. Watch me, %1$s.
Careful — encourage me and I might drag you along.
That's kind. But dreams cost coin, and mine's mostly spoken for.
dialogue.conversations.dreams.more: More? Alright. In the dream there's a porch, and nobody needs anything from me until noon.
dialogue.conversations.fears.first: Honestly? Thunder. And the thing that scratched at my door two winters back. Mostly the thunder.
dialogue.conversations.fears.first/1: Being forgotten. Everyone remembers the mayor. Nobody remembers who fixed the well.
dialogue.conversations.fears.first/2: The dark past the last lantern. Everyone pretends they're not afraid of it. They're lying.
dialogue.conversations.fears.revisit: I've been chewing on what you asked me — about being afraid. It's lighter now that it's said.
dialogue.conversations.fears.again: I already showed you that scar, %1$s. Don't poke it twice in one week.
dialogue.conversations.fears.challenge: You could face it. I'd stand with you.
dialogue.conversations.fears.press: Tell me the rest of it.
dialogue.conversations.fears.comfort.cri: ...You mean that. You're not just being polite. Then here's the part I never say out loud: it's worse when nobody knows. It's smaller already.
Careful, %1$s. Kindness like that makes a person start hoping. ...Too late. Hoping.
dialogue.conversations.fears.comfort.reb: Don't. I didn't hand you that so you could pat it on the head.
Soft words, %1$s? It isn't a soft thing. Leave it be.
dialogue.conversations.fears.challenge.g: That's easy to say from where you're standing. We're not there yet, you and I.
Face it. Just like that. ...Know a person before you volunteer them for bravery, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.fears.challenge.c: ...Nobody ever offered the 'with you' part before. That's the part that matters. Alright. Next time it comes, I don't run. Witnessed.
You'd actually stand there with me. Huh. — Fine. I'm holding you to it, and you're holding me to it.
dialogue.conversations.fears.challenge.s: Maybe. With a witness, maybe. Don't let me back out of it later.
You make it sound almost possible. Ask me again when it's close, and we'll learn what I'm made of.
dialogue.conversations.fears.challenge.p: Easy for you — you've got somewhere else to be when it goes wrong. ...But it wasn't nothing, you offering.
Hm. Half of me believes you. The other half keeps the accounts.
dialogue.conversations.fears.challenge.r: Don't make my fear a test of your character, %1$s. It isn't yours to be brave about.
Stand with me? You'll be gone by frost like everyone else. No.
dialogue.conversations.fears.press.guard: The rest isn't for sale, %1$s. It's not even for borrowing. Not yet.
There's a door in that story I don't open for acquaintances. No offense meant.
dialogue.conversations.fears.press.crit: ...You don't flinch, do you. Alright. The rest — the true shape of it, the part I skip even alone at night. Sit down. I've never told anyone this.
dialogue.conversations.fears.press.crit/: Persistent. And gentle about it, which is worse. ...Fine. The whole of it, then. But it stays between us, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.fears.press.succe: There's more, yes. Give me a breath. ...There. Now two of us are carrying it, and it's strange how much lighter that is.
You pull gently, I'll give you that. All right — a little more of it. The rest another day.
dialogue.conversations.fears.press.parti: Some of it, maybe. Not tonight. Tonight's too much like the night it happened.
That thread's still attached to something, %1$s. Later. I mean it — later, not never.
dialogue.conversations.fears.press.rebuf: I said what I said. The rest is mine. Leave it.
No. Some doors you don't knock on twice in a day, %1$s. I'd have thought you knew that.
dialogue.conversations.fears.comfort.tha: ...Thank you. Most people change the subject.
dialogue.conversations.fears.comfort.bru: I'm fine. Forget I said anything. The thunder and I have an understanding.
dialogue.conversations.fears.share.grate: You too? Huh. It's less heavy when two people carry it.
Strange comfort, that. Two cowards make one brave pair.
dialogue.conversations.fears.share.joke: Then we'll hide under the same table when it storms. Bring bread.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.first: You're really asking? Fine. You're the part of my day I don't complain about.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.first/1: I notice when you don't come around. That's my answer.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.spouse: You're my whole ledger, %1$s. Every column. Even the messy ones.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.spouse/1: Married you, didn't I? But since you're asking — I'd do it again tomorrow.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.again: I laid my heart on the table already. Give it a day to recover.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.unsure: I'm not sure how I feel yet.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.same.hap: Then say it more often, %1$s. Words like that keep better than bread.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.same.shy: Oh. I... need to go stand somewhere else and smile for a bit.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.unsure.h: Right. Well. Thank you for the honesty, I suppose.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.unsure.p: That's fair. I'm not going anywhere. Take your time.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.first: One or two. There was a door I didn't knock on, years ago. I still walk past it.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.first/1: I regret the things I didn't say at a funeral once. Say your things, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.first/2: I traded a friendship for pride once. Worst deal I ever made.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.again: We turned those stones over already. Let them lie a while.
dialogue.conversations.deflect.personal: That's... a bit close to the bone for someone I barely know.
dialogue.conversations.deflect.personal/: Maybe when I know you better, %1$s. Words like that need trust first.
Buy me a sweetroll first. Then we'll see about the deep questions.
I keep that shelf locked. Come back when we're friends, not acquaintances.
dialogue.conversations.deflect.intimate: That question belongs to someone I trust with everything. We're not there.
dialogue.conversations.deflect.intimate/: Ask me again when you've earned it, %1$s. That one costs more than hearts on a sleeve.
Some doors open slowly. Keep showing up and maybe.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.marriage: You didn't hear it from me, but %2$s and %3$s got married! The whole square's been buzzing.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.marriage/1: Big news — %2$s finally married %3$s. About time, if you ask anyone with eyes.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.marriage/2: %2$s and %3$s tied the knot, %1$s. There wasn't a dry eye or an empty cup by the end of it.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.divorce: Keep it quiet, but %2$s and %3$s split up. Nobody's saying why and everybody's guessing.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.divorce/1: %2$s and %3$s aren't together anymore. The baker knew before either of them did, I swear.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.divorce/2: Word is %2$s and %3$s have parted ways. Sad business. I'll not take sides where I can help it.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.death: Sad news, I'm afraid. We lost %2$s. The village feels smaller without them.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.death/1: You heard about %2$s? Gone. Folks left flowers by the well.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.death/2: We buried %2$s this week, %1$s. A hard thing. We look out for each other a little closer now.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.birth: Happy news for once — there's a new baby! Little %2$s. Loudest lungs in the village.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.birth/1: Have you seen the baby yet? %2$s. Even the grumpy ones stopped to smile.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.birth/2: A little one arrived — %2$s. The whole village has gone soft over the cradle, myself included.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.arrival: We've a new face about — %2$s moved in not long ago. Still finding their way round the lanes.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.arrival/1: Did you meet %2$s yet? Just settled here. Give them a wave, they're a bit lost still.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.arrival/2: Fresh blood in the village, %1$s — %2$s came to stay. Always good to see the place growing.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.departure: You won't find %2$s here anymore — packed up and moved on. Odd, seeing their door shut for good.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.departure/: %2$s left us. No goodbye to speak of. The village feels a touch quieter for it.
Heard %2$s moved away, %1$s. Folk do, now and then. Still, you notice the gap.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.quest: Did you hear? %2$s had a proper bit of help lately. Word gets around.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.quest/1: Folk are saying %2$s finally got that trouble sorted. Good for them.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.quest/2: Between us, %1$s — %2$s owes someone a favour now. Small village, big ears.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.none: Quiet week, honestly. The most exciting thing was a chicken on the chapel roof.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.none/1: Nothing new. Same faces, same fences. I'd trade an ear for some real news.
dialogue.conversations.quest.offer: Since you ask, %1$s — aye, there's a thing or two. Let me show you what I need.
dialogue.conversations.quest.offer/1: Funny you should ask, %1$s. I do have something that wants doing.
dialogue.conversations.quest.offer/2: As it happens, %1$s, there's work if you want it. Here, take a look.
dialogue.conversations.quest.none: Nothing needs doing right now, %1$s. But I appreciate you asking.
dialogue.conversations.quest.none/1: All's handled for the moment, %1$s. Come back and I might have work.
dialogue.conversations.quest.none/2: No, %1$s, I'm caught up. Kind of you to offer, though.
dialogue.conversations.quest.accepted: You're taking on %2$s? You're a good sort, %1$s. I won't forget it.
dialogue.conversations.quest.accepted/1: %1$s, thank you. %2$s has been weighing on me.
dialogue.conversations.quest.accepted/2: Bless you, %1$s. Get %2$s sorted and I'll make it worth your while.
dialogue.conversations.quest.in_progress: %2$s — still on it, %1$s? No rush. Well, some rush.
dialogue.conversations.quest.ready: You've done it? Let me see — %2$s, finished! Wonderful, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.quest.ready/1: Is that %2$s done already? %1$s, you're a marvel.
dialogue.conversations.quest.ready/2: Ha! %2$s, sorted. Come here, %1$s, let me thank you proper.
dialogue.conversations.quest.completed: That's %2$s put to bed. Thank you, %1$s — truly.
dialogue.conversations.quest.completed/1: Good and done. I owe you for %2$s, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.quest.completed/2: %2$s, finished and dusted. You've my thanks, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.quest.failed: Ah… %2$s didn't work out. Don't dwell on it, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.quest.failed/1: So %2$s slipped away. It happens, %1$s. Chin up.
dialogue.conversations.quest.failed/2: %1$s, %2$s went sideways. We'll manage. We always do.
dialogue.conversations.us.future: What do you want for our future?
dialogue.conversations.us.happy.yes: With you? Yes. Even when you track mud in. Especially then, somehow.
dialogue.conversations.us.happy.yes/1: I catch myself humming while I work. That's your fault, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.us.happy.low: I'm happy with you. It's everything else that's been heavy lately.
dialogue.conversations.us.happy.grateful: Happy? You brought me %2$s and asked me that with a straight face. Yes, love. Yes.
Still smiling about that %2$s, if I'm honest. You know me too well.
dialogue.conversations.us.firstmet.memor: Of course. You looked completely lost, and I pretended I wasn't staring. Best day %2$s ever had.
You had the wrong boots for the weather and the right smile for me. I remember all of it.
dialogue.conversations.us.firstmet.again: We just walked down that road, love. But I never mind the view.
dialogue.conversations.us.future.togethe: More mornings like this one. Maybe a bigger table. People to sit at it.
I want us old and insufferable on a porch somewhere, judging everyone's fences.
dialogue.conversations.us.future.baby: Right now? I mostly think about the little one coming. Terrified. Thrilled. Both.
dialogue.conversations.us.future.kids: I want the kids to have it easier than we did. That's the whole plan, really.
dialogue.conversations.us.worries.open: Since you ask... yes. I didn't want to burden you, but yes. Sit with me a moment.
dialogue.conversations.us.worries.open/1: There's a weight I've been carrying quietly. I should have told you sooner.
dialogue.conversations.us.worries.fine: Nothing worth your frown. The usual aches. Having you ask is half the cure.
dialogue.conversations.us.worries.again: You checked on me already, love. I promise I'd tell you.
dialogue.conversations.family.checkin_ch: How are you holding up, little one?
dialogue.conversations.family.ask_parent: Can I ask you something? Parent to child?
dialogue.conversations.family.child.litt: Up! Up! I found a bug and it's my friend now!
I'm gonna be tall tomorrow. I decided.
dialogue.conversations.family.child.teen: I'm fine. Everyone keeps asking. I'm FINE. ...Thanks for asking, though.
Can I have more responsibility and also no responsibility? Is that a thing?
dialogue.conversations.family.child.doin: Pretty good! I beat the miller's kid at races twice. TWICE.
dialogue.conversations.family.parent.pro: You turned out well, you know. I don't say it enough. I'm saying it now.
Ask away. Though watching you lately, you need less advice than you think.
dialogue.conversations.family.parent.wor: I worry, that's all. It's the job. You never stop being someone's parent.
dialogue.conversations.family.memories.s: Did I ever tell you about the winter %2$s got snowed into the outhouse? No? Sit down.
There's a story about %2$s and a runaway pig that this family swore to keep secret. Anyway—
dialogue.conversations.family.memories.a: I told you the good one already. The rest need supper and a fire to come out right.
dialogue.main/9: I've got a few minutes before someone needs something.
dialogue.main/11: You've got that look. What is it this time?
dialogue.main/12: Talk to me. The turnips can wait.
dialogue.greet.success/6: There's a face I don't mind seeing.
dialogue.greet.success/7: Morning, noon, whatever it is — good to see you, %1$s.
dialogue.greet.success/8: Well met. You picked a fine day to exist.
dialogue.greet.success/9: Ah, %1$s! I was just thinking the day needed improving.
dialogue.greet.fail/6: Oh. It's you. I was hoping for the bread cart.
dialogue.greet.fail/8: If this is about the fence, I already know.
dialogue.story.success/10: One more? Alright — the year the river froze solid, we bowled with pumpkins on it.
dialogue.story.success/11: Did I tell you about the trader who sold maps to places he invented? Half the village still owns one.
dialogue.story.success/12: There was a rooster here once so mean it had its own warning sign. True story.
dialogue.story.success/13: My grandmother could predict rain with her knees. Never wrong. Terrifying woman.
dialogue.shake_hand.success/6: Firm grip! You'd survive market day.
dialogue.shake_hand.success/7: A proper handshake. Rarer than emeralds these days.
dialogue.shake_hand.success/8: Deal's a deal, whatever we just agreed to.
dialogue.conversations/3: Alright, you have my attention. All of it, even.
dialogue.conversations/4: Pull up a fence post. What's on your mind?
dialogue.conversations.deflect.personal/: You get the weather and the crops, %1$s. The rest costs friendship.
My mother said never hand a stranger your heart or your ladder. I lost the ladder that way.
dialogue.conversations.deflect.intimate/: There are maybe two people alive who get that answer. Working on whether you're the third.
Not yet. And 'yet' is doing a lot of kind work in that sentence.
dialogue.conversations.deflect.secret: Secrets are traded, not given. Trust me with something of yours first.
dialogue.conversations.deflect.secret/1: You first, %1$s. That's how secrets work.
dialogue.conversations.deflect.secret/2: When you've told me something that matters, I'll match it. That's the deal.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.again/2: Persistent today, aren't we? Same answer, warmer delivery.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.rough/2: I've been carrying more than my basket lately. It shows, huh?
dialogue.conversations.day.again/2: The day refuses to get more interesting, I'm afraid.
dialogue.conversations.day.rough/2: I dropped an egg, then a bucket, then my patience. In that order.
dialogue.conversations.day.working/2: You've caught me mid-chore. Talk while I work — the wood doesn't judge.
dialogue.conversations.dreams.again/1: My dream hasn't changed since this morning, %1$s. They move slower than that.
dialogue.conversations.dreams.again/2: Still the same dream. Still saving up for it.
You sound like my grandmother. She was usually right, which is the annoying part.
Easy for you to say — you've seen the world past the wheat line.
Say that again sometime. It works better than coffee.
dialogue.conversations.dreams.more/1: There's a second part I don't tell everyone. There's a dog in it. A big, useless, happy one.
dialogue.conversations.dreams.more/2: Details? In the dream nobody knocks on my door before breakfast. Pure fantasy.
dialogue.conversations.dreams.revisit/1: You remembered my dream? Careful, %1$s, I might start believing in it again.
dialogue.conversations.dreams.revisit/2: Since you asked last time, I've saved four emeralds toward it. Four! It begins.
dialogue.conversations.family.child.doin: Good! I taught the cat to sit. It sat for entirely unrelated reasons but STILL.
I grew this much since you last asked! At least this much.
dialogue.conversations.family.child.litt: I ate a flower today. Don't tell the flower.
dialogue.conversations.family.memories.a: You've had your story for the week. Family rates apply.
Later. A story told twice too soon goes stale like bread.
dialogue.conversations.family.memories.s: Ask %2$s about the beehive someday. Watch their face. That's the whole story right there.
dialogue.conversations.family.parent.pro: Whatever you're about to ask — yes, I'm proud of you. Now what was it?
dialogue.conversations.family.parent.wor: You look thinner. Are you eating? Don't make that face, it's my job to ask.
I still check the door at night wondering if you're safe out there. Old habit.
dialogue.conversations.fears.again/1: Twice in one week you want my nightmares? Buy me a drink first.
dialogue.conversations.fears.again/2: Let that one rest, %1$s. It bites when it's poked fresh.
dialogue.conversations.fears.comfort.bru: Yes, well. Enough about that. How's the weather treating you?
Don't make it a thing. It's not a thing. It's a perfectly reasonable dread.
dialogue.conversations.fears.comfort.tha: Funny how a fear shrinks a little every time somebody doesn't laugh at it.
dialogue.conversations.fears.revisit/1: That fear we talked about — I slept with the lantern out twice this week. Progress.
dialogue.conversations.fears.revisit/2: I keep coming back to what you asked. Naming a thing takes some of its teeth.
dialogue.conversations.fears.share.joke/: Excellent. You bring the bread, I'll bring the trembling.
A matched set of cowards! The village should charge admission.
dialogue.conversations.fears.share.grate: Then we watch each other's backs. That's how it's supposed to work anyway.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.again/1: My heart's still where it was an hour ago, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.again/2: Don't spend a good answer twice in one day. Let it earn interest.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.first/2: When you leave, the room gets quieter than it should. Make of that what you will.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.same.hap: Well. Now I have to go tell the chickens. They gossip worse than the baker.
Good. GOOD. I mean — good. Very casual about this. Extremely casual.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.same.shy: I— yes. Same. I need to go count something now.
Oh no. Oh no, that's wonderful. Excuse me while my face catches fire.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.spouse/2: I chose you on purpose, %1$s. I keep choosing you every morning since.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.unsure.h: Mm. That lands about as soft as an anvil, but I asked for honest.
I see. Well. The turnips still need me, even if the answer's a maybe.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.unsure.p: Hearts keep their own calendars. I can wait through a season or two.
Fair enough. I'm patient like winter — I always come back around.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.none/2: All quiet. Even the baker's out of scandals, and that's saying something.
dialogue.conversations.life.again/1: My whole biography twice in one week? Wait for the second edition.
dialogue.conversations.life.again/2: You know the story now, %1$s. Nothing's happened since except lunch.
dialogue.conversations.life.revisit/2: Been sorting through the years since we talked. Some of them were better than I let on.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.again/1: One airing per season for those, %1$s. Doctor's orders. I'm the doctor.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.again/2: We buried those stones together already. Let the grass grow over them a while.
dialogue.conversations.us.firstmet.again: Again? Alright — you were lost, I was smitten. Short version this time.
We told this one already, love. It gets ten percent more heroic every telling.
dialogue.conversations.us.firstmet.memor: I remember the exact spot. I walk past it some mornings just to smile at nothing.
dialogue.conversations.us.future.baby/1: I keep talking to the little one. Mostly apologies for the world, and one good joke.
dialogue.conversations.us.future.baby/2: A name. We need a name, and the courage to argue about it kindly.
dialogue.conversations.us.future.kids/1: I want the kids to inherit a full pantry and none of my stubbornness. Half's likely.
dialogue.conversations.us.future.kids/2: Watching them grow is the future. Everything else is furniture.
dialogue.conversations.us.future.togethe: A garden big enough to argue about. That's the dream, and you're in it.
dialogue.conversations.us.happy.grateful: Between you and that %2$s, I've run clean out of complaints. It's disorienting.
dialogue.conversations.us.happy.low/1: You're the good part, love. The rest of it has just been raining sideways lately.
dialogue.conversations.us.happy.low/2: With us? Always. With everything around us? Ask me after a nap.
dialogue.conversations.us.happy.yes/2: Happy enough to hum. And you know how I feel about people who hum.
dialogue.conversations.us.worries.again/: Still fine, love. Checking twice doesn't double the answer.
If something were wrong, you'd hear it through the wall before you asked.
dialogue.conversations.us.worries.fine/1: Just the knees and the weather. Both complain, neither listens.
dialogue.conversations.us.worries.fine/2: Nothing today. Keep asking though — someday the answer changes, and I'd want it to be you.
dialogue.conversations.us.worries.open/2: There is something. I've been rehearsing how to say it for a week. Sit with me.
dialogue.conversations.village.again/1: The village hasn't moved since you asked, %1$s. I checked.
dialogue.conversations.village.again/2: Same bell, same gossip, same crack in the well. Comforting, in its way.
dialogue.conversations.village.home/2: %2$s raised me, fed me, and talks about me behind my back. Family, basically.
dialogue.conversations.village.none/2: Home is wherever my boots stop hurting. Haven't found it yet.
dialogue.conversations.work.again/1: The job's the same as it was this morning, %1$s. Reliable that way.
dialogue.conversations.work.again/2: Ask the work how it likes ME for a change.
dialogue.conversations.work.hate/2: Don't tell the mayor, but some days I do the whole job out of pure spite.
dialogue.conversations.work.generic: Being a %2$s isn't glamorous, but it's mine, and I'm better at it than most.
dialogue.conversations.work.generic/1: A %2$s's day starts before the sun and ends after the complaints. I'd still choose it.
dialogue.conversations.work.generic/2: Somebody in this village has to be the %2$s. Turns out somebody is me.
dialogue.conversations.food.first: The baker's rye, fresh, with too much butter. That's the correct answer and I'll die on it.
dialogue.conversations.food.first/1: Stew night at the inn. Get there early or fight the blacksmith for the last bowl. He wins.
dialogue.conversations.food.first/2: Anything I didn't have to cook myself tastes better. It's science.
dialogue.conversations.food.again: Still hungry from the last time you asked, honestly.
dialogue.conversations.food.again/1: We just talked food and now I want bread again. See what you've done?
dialogue.conversations.food.again/2: My answer's the same, my stomach agrees, and it's nearly mealtime. Coincidence?
dialogue.conversations.food.revisit: I thought about what you asked — I tried the mushroom thing. I was wrong about mushrooms.
dialogue.conversations.food.revisit/1: Since you asked last, the baker changed the rye recipe. The village is split. Families divided.
dialogue.conversations.food.revisit/2: Been cooking more since we talked food. The smoke alarm is a kettle I hit with a spoon.
dialogue.conversations.food.trait.vegeta: No meat for me — never touch it. The pigs and I have an arrangement built on trust.
I don't eat anything with a face. The garden feeds me fine, and nothing in it screams.
dialogue.conversations.food.trait.lactos: Keep the milk away from me, %1$s. Learned that lesson in front of the whole market. Twice.
Cheese and I are old enemies. It always wins, and everyone downwind loses.
dialogue.conversations.food.trait.coelia: Bread hates me. Actual bread. In a village that's half bakery. The gods have humor.
No wheat for me — one roll and I'm bedridden. I smell the bakery like other folk visit museums.
dialogue.conversations.food.trait.diabet: I have to watch the sweets. One cookie, the cleric says. Who bakes ONE cookie?
Sugar's rationed for me these days. I trade my desserts for gossip. Better for the heart anyway.
dialogue.conversations.food.trait.sirben: The sirben feast on the night wind, %1$s. We do not speak of the recipe. HRRK.
dialogue.conversations.people.first: Good folk, mostly. We share fences, weather, and opinions about each other. It works.
dialogue.conversations.people.first/1: You live close enough to anyone, you learn their sneezes by name. I know everyone's sneeze.
dialogue.conversations.people.first/2: The neighbors? We feud gently and forgive quickly. Village rules.
dialogue.conversations.people.again: I said my piece about the neighbors. Any more and it becomes gossip, which is a different question.
dialogue.conversations.people.again/1: Careful, %1$s — twice in a week and people start thinking YOU'RE the nosy one.
dialogue.conversations.people.again/2: Nothing's changed since you asked. Same saints, same menaces.
dialogue.conversations.people.revisit: You asked about the neighbors once. I've warmed up on a couple of them since. Slightly.
dialogue.conversations.people.revisit/1: Been watching folk differently since we talked. Everyone's carrying something, turns out.
dialogue.conversations.people.revisit/2: Since you asked last — the miller apologized. I nearly fainted into the flour.
dialogue.conversations.people.warm: I love them. All of them. Even the loud ones. ESPECIALLY the loud ones.
dialogue.conversations.people.warm/1: This village is one big family that argues about fences. I wouldn't trade a single one.
dialogue.conversations.people.warm/2: Every door here would open for me at midnight if I knocked. That's wealth, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.people.judgy: Half of them owe me favors and the other half owe me apologies. I keep a list.
dialogue.conversations.people.judgy/1: Fine people, if you like noise, borrowed tools that never return, and opinions at dawn.
dialogue.conversations.people.judgy/2: I'd rank them, but you'd repeat it, and then I'd have to rank you too.
dialogue.conversations.people.shy: They're... a lot. Kind, but a lot. I like them best from my window, waving.
dialogue.conversations.people.shy/1: Everyone's lovely. I just need three days' notice and an escape route to enjoy them.
dialogue.conversations.people.shy/2: I know them all by footstep. It saves having to look up.
dialogue.conversations.people.wry: A finer collection of characters was never assembled on purpose. Note: it wasn't on purpose.
dialogue.conversations.people.wry/1: The neighbors are free theater, %1$s. The matinee is the market. Bring snacks.
dialogue.conversations.people.wry/2: Decent souls. Odd hats. The correlation is real and I'm studying it.
dialogue.conversations.secret.first: Alright. You've earned one. The 'famous' pie I bring to festivals? The trader sells it to me. Every year.
dialogue.conversations.secret.first/1: Come closer. I've never once liked the mayor's speeches. I clap because the baker watches. THAT stays here.
dialogue.conversations.secret.first/2: One secret, because it's you: there's a loose brick behind the well with my rainy-day emeralds. Now two of us know.
dialogue.conversations.secret.again: One secret per season, %1$s. Any faster and they stop being secrets.
dialogue.conversations.secret.again/1: You've had your secret. I'm still nervous about the last one.
dialogue.conversations.secret.again/2: Greedy! Secrets need time to grow back, like carrots. Dark, private carrots.
dialogue.conversations.secret.revisit: Still keeping what I told you? ...Good. Then maybe there's another where that came from, someday.
dialogue.conversations.secret.revisit/1: You never breathed a word about last time. I noticed. I don't forget that kind of quiet.
dialogue.conversations.secret.revisit/2: Since you kept the last one — the loose brick has a second brick. That's all I'm saying today.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.toddler: I'm good! I found a bug this morning. It wiggled.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.toddler/2: I got up ALL by myself today.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.child: Good! Mostly good. The goat and I have a truce now.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.child/1: I'm okay! I only fell in the pond once this whole week.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.teen: Fine, I guess. Same as yesterday.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.teen/1: Busy. Everyone suddenly wants me to do chores.
dialogue.conversations.day.toddler: I stacked mud! It was the best mud.
dialogue.conversations.day.toddler/1: Today is SO long. Is it snack time?
dialogue.conversations.day.toddler/2: I chased a butterfly and then it chased ME.
dialogue.conversations.food.toddler: I like bread. And apples. And bread.
dialogue.conversations.food.toddler/1: Sweet berries! But not the squishy ones.
dialogue.conversations.food.toddler/2: Mama cuts mine into little pieces so it tastes better.
dialogue.conversations.food.child: Cookies first, THEN bread. That's the right order and nobody listens.
dialogue.conversations.food.child/1: I tried a beetroot once. Once.
dialogue.conversations.food.teen: Whatever's in the pantry when nobody's looking.
dialogue.conversations.food.teen/1: Bread's fine. I'm not picky anymore, I'm just hungry.
dialogue.conversations.weather.toddler: Sky water! I like jumping in the puddles after.
dialogue.conversations.weather.toddler/1: The clouds look like sheep today. Big sky sheep.
dialogue.conversations.weather.toddler/2: Is it gonna thunder? I'm not scared. Maybe a little.
dialogue.conversations.season.toddler: I like the season where the flowers come. Is it that one?
dialogue.conversations.season.toddler/1: Leaves! There are SO many leaves.
dialogue.conversations.season.toddler/2: Every day is puddle season if you believe.
dialogue.conversations.village.toddler: I like it here! My house is here and my toys are here.
dialogue.conversations.village.toddler/1: The village is big. I'm not allowed past the well.
dialogue.conversations.village.toddler/2: This is the best village 'cause I live in it.
dialogue.conversations.village.child: It's good! I know all the shortcuts. ALL of them.
dialogue.conversations.village.child/1: Home's great — the baker waves at me and sometimes there are extra rolls.
dialogue.conversations.village.teen: It's small. Everyone knows everything about everyone.
dialogue.conversations.village.teen/1: It's home. Bit quiet. That's fine, I guess.
dialogue.conversations.people.child: The miller's kid is my best friend except on race days.
dialogue.conversations.people.child/1: Everyone's nice! Except when they're telling me to slow down.
dialogue.conversations.people.teen: They're fine. Everybody's got opinions about my hair, though.
dialogue.conversations.life.toddler: I'm little! I do puddles and snacks and naps. It's a full day.
dialogue.conversations.life.toddler/1: My life is good. Yesterday I saw a frog.
dialogue.conversations.life.toddler/2: When I'm big I'll reach the table. The WHOLE table.
dialogue.conversations.life.child: School, chores, and expert-level puddle finding.
dialogue.conversations.life.child/1: I'm learning to whittle! I've made three sticks into... pointier sticks.
dialogue.conversations.life.teen/1: I'm figuring things out. Slowly. Don't rush me.
dialogue.conversations.dreams.toddler/1: A pony! Or a dog. Or a pony-dog.
dialogue.conversations.dreams.toddler/2: I dreamed I was a bee last night. It was great.
dialogue.conversations.fears.toddler: The dark under the bed. There's a WHOLE nothing under there.
dialogue.conversations.fears.toddler/1: Thunder. But only the loud kind.
dialogue.conversations.fears.toddler/2: When Mama hides her face behind her hands. Where does she GO?
dialogue.conversations.hopes.toddler: Snacks tomorrow! And the day after!
dialogue.conversations.hopes.toddler/1: I hope the frog comes back. He's my friend.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.toddler/2: Being big! With pockets. Lots of pockets.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.child: I hope I get my own fishing rod this year. A real one.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.child/1: I'm hoping for a dog. I've been very convincing.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.teen: To get out of chores... and maybe see the next village over someday.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.teen/1: Honestly? A day where nobody needs me for anything.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.toddler: I feel... hungry. And a little like dancing.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.toddler/: Happy! 'Cept my sock has a hole. So mostly happy.
I dunno. Warm? Is warm a feeling?
dialogue.conversations.feelings.child: Good! Unless it's bath day. Then betrayed.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.child/1: I'm happy when I'm outside and grumpy when I'm not. Simple.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.teen: That's kind of personal. ...Fine. Bit stormy lately, alright?
dialogue.conversations.feelings.teen/1: I'm FINE. Why does everyone keep checking?
dialogue.conversations.family.memories.t: 'Member when we saw the sheep? That was the best day of my LIFE.
One time you were here and I showed you my rock. You 'member.
I remember breakfast. It was good.
dialogue.conversations.work.child: My job is being a kid and I'm SO good at it.
dialogue.conversations.work.child/1: I help the grown-ups sometimes! Mostly I supervise.
dialogue.conversations.work.teen: Bit of everything — whatever the grown-ups don't want to do, apparently.
dialogue.conversations.work.teen/1: Still 'finding my calling'. Today my calling was hauling firewood.
dialogue.conversations.day.child: BEST day. I found a rock shaped like a slightly different rock!
dialogue.conversations.day.child/1: I raced the chickens and only lost twice. They cheat with the flapping.
dialogue.conversations.day.teen: It's fine. It's a day. They keep happening whether I approve or not.
dialogue.conversations.day.teen/1: Chores, chores, being told I'm 'so grown up now', more chores. Riveting.
dialogue.conversations.dreams.child: I'm gonna be a knight AND a baker. Sword in one hand, cake in the other. It's decided.
dialogue.conversations.dreams.child/1: I want a pet slime! A LITTLE one. It can sleep in the boot box.
dialogue.conversations.dreams.teen: Somewhere that isn't here, doing something nobody assigned me. That's the whole dream so far.
dialogue.conversations.dreams.teen/1: Don't laugh — I've been practicing the bow when nobody's watching. I'm getting good.
dialogue.conversations.fears.child: The under-the-bed place. Papa checked it but monsters KNOW when papas leave.
dialogue.conversations.fears.child/1: Thunder. But only the loud kind. The rumbly kind is the sky's tummy and that's fine.
dialogue.conversations.fears.teen: That I'll end up exactly like everyone here and never find out what else I could've been.
dialogue.conversations.fears.teen/1: Honestly? Disappointing people. I act like I don't care. I care the most.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.farmer: Farming's honest: you plant, you pray, you pull weeds. The weeds always negotiate hardest.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.farmer/: I talk to the crops, %1$s. The wheat listens. The beetroot is a lost cause.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.fisherm: The fish and I have an understanding: I wait, they mock me, occasionally one apologizes into the net.
Best office in the village — the dock at dawn. Worst coworker — the heron. He steals.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.shepher: The flock knows me better than most people do. Sheep don't gossip. Much.
Shearing season is one long argument I have with forty woolly lawyers.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.fletche: Every arrow that flies true is a small promise kept. I keep hundreds a week.
Feathers, shafts, patience. Mostly patience. The guard breaks them faster than I fletch them.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.librari: I mind the books. They mind me back. Quieter company than the tavern and twice as opinionated.
People think it's dull work. Those people have never smelled a new-bound book, and I pity them.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.cartogr: I draw the world so nobody gets lost the way I once did. Every map is a small rescue.
The edges of the map are my favorite part. That's where the excuses to travel live.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.cleric: I tend souls and brew what mends them. Half my job is listening. You'd be surprised who talks.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.cleric/: Between the candles and the confessions, I hear this village's whole heart. It's a good heart. Mostly.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.armorer: I make the steel that stands between folk and their bad luck. Heavy work. Sleeps well, though.
Every dent in a breastplate I made is a funeral that didn't happen. I count them proudly.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.weapons: Blades are honest tools — they only ever do what the hand asks. I try to like the hands I sell to.
The forge doesn't care about your feelings, which is exactly what I like about it.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.toolsmi: Shovels, hoes, picks — unglamorous things that build everything. Somebody has to make the quiet heroes.
A good tool outlives its maker. I'm leaving this village a hundred small immortalities.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.butcher: It's blunt work, but nobody in this village goes hungry on my watch. That's the whole ethics of it.
The cleaver and I feed the village. The vegetarian glares at me across the square. We manage.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.leather: Hides come in stiff and ornery, leave soft and useful. There's a sermon in that if you want one.
Everything I make gets better with age and wear. I aspire to the same.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.mason: Stone is patient and so am I. The wall I built at twenty will outlive my grandchildren's grudges.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.mason/1: People see rock. I see the corner of a house where somebody's whole life will happen.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.nitwit: Work? Oh, I supervise. The clouds, mostly. Somebody has to make sure they keep moving.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.nitwit/: I tried a job once. Terrible fit. My true calling is being a cautionary tale, and business is BOOMING.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.none: No trade yet — I'm between destinies. The lean season of a life, my gran called it.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.none/1: No master, no bell, no bench. Poor as dirt and free as weather. Ask me again next season.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.guard: I hold the wall so everyone else gets to complain about smaller things. It's good work.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.guard/1: Quiet shifts are the victory, %1$s. Nobody thanks you for the monster that never arrived.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.archer: From the tower I see everything — who's brave, who's sneaking, whose roof needs mending. Mostly roofs.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.archer/: One arrow, one warning. I haven't needed a second in years, and I practice so I never do.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.adventu: The road's my trade. I rest here between chapters — villages are where adventurers footnote themselves.
I've seen the nether's ceiling and the ocean's floor. The scariest thing is still an empty food bag.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.mercena: Coin for steel, steel for coin. I keep my contracts and my blade clean. One of those is hard.
Don't romanticize it, %1$s. It's a job with worse weather and better stories.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.cultist: We are a BOOK CLUB. A perfectly ordinary book club. The chanting is... enthusiasm for literature.
The stars whisper such things, %1$s. Would you like a pamphlet? Everyone eventually takes a pamphlet.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.outlaw: My line of work is... freelance redistribution. The mayor and I disagree on the terminology.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.outlaw/: Every village needs someone the sermons can point at. I provide a vital service.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.enderia: I study the tall ones and their pearls. Rule one: notes, never eye contact. Rule two: see rule one.
The end is less empty than people think, %1$s. Something out there stares back. I take notes.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.enginee: Redstone, pistons, the occasional explosion — I prefer 'rapid disassembly'. Progress has a sound.
Everyone laughs at the twitching contraption until it waters their crops for them. Then it's 'genius'.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.florist: Flowers are the only customers that never complain. The bees drive a hard bargain, though.
Every bouquet is somebody's apology, courtship, or funeral. I arrange the whole human heart in stems.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.hunter: I read the woods like the librarian reads books. Tracks don't lie. People, occasionally.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.hunter/: The forest feeds us if you ask it right and thank it after. Most folk skip both steps.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.miner: Down in the dark you learn what you're made of. Mostly I'm made of dust and stubbornness.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.miner/1: Every torch I plant is a little argument against the dark. I'm winning by about ten thousand.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.netheri: I map the red place. Yes, the burning one. My eyebrows grow back faster than you'd think.
The nether has rules, %1$s. Learn them and it's almost hospitable. Forget one and you're a headline.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.oceanog: The sea keeps better secrets than any of us. I've surfaced with a few. Traded most for dry socks.
People fear the deep. The deep is fine. It's the surprise guardians that season the workday.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.woodwor: Trees give a lifetime of patience in every plank. I try to build things worthy of the wait.
I can tell any beam's tree by the grain. The tavern bar? That was a spiteful old oak. Fitting.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.shady_w: I sell... solutions. Magical ones. No refunds, no questions, and definitely no warranty cards.
'Shady' is such a harsh word, %1$s. I prefer 'discounted arcana, sourced creatively'.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.delight: A proper kitchen is a battlefield that ends in dessert. I run mine like a loving tyrant.
Anyone can fill a stomach. My job is making the blacksmith close his eyes at the first bite. Got him twice.
I feed the village the food it needs, not the food it deserves. There are vegetables hidden in everything.
Stew's a mercy, bread's a promise, and nobody leaves my pot line hungry. House rules.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.scribe: I copy what the dragons leave behind — words older than kingdoms. My ink hand shakes for good reason.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.scribe/: Every manuscript I save is a candle lit against forgetting. Some of them bite, mind you.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.hunter_: I train those who stand against the night-drinkers. Garlic inventory alone is a full day's work.
The pay is poor and the hours are worse, but somebody has to teach the stakes. Literally, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.priest: I keep the faith and the holy water stocked. In this region, both run out faster than you'd hope.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.priest/: My sermons cover the usual: kindness, patience, and what to do if your neighbor stops casting a reflection.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.vampire: I advise on... nocturnal affairs. Professionally. My clientele tips well and never comes by at noon.
Knowledge of the blood arts is just knowledge, %1$s. It's the appetite you have to interview for.
dialogue.conversations.work.prof.werewol: I consult on the moon-touched. The trick is scheduling around the calendar. THEIR calendar.
Fur, fangs, phases — manageable, all of it, with preparation. The unprepared become anecdotes.
dialogue.chat: Oh, a proper conversation? Alright then. Go on.
dialogue.chat/1: You've got the look of someone with questions. Out with them.
dialogue.chat/2: Talk? Gladly. The fence posts never answer back.
dialogue.chat/3: Sure, I've a moment. Maybe two if it's interesting.
dialogue.chat/4: Well now. What shall we untangle today, %1$s?
dialogue.conversations.cat.chitchat.weat: What do you make of this weather?
dialogue.conversations.cat.events.notice: How have you been, in yourself?
dialogue.conversations.weather.storm: Wild sky today. I've got the shutters latched and a candle ready. Best stay in if you can, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.weather.storm/1: Thunder like that, the animals won't settle and neither will I. Mind the lightning out there.
dialogue.conversations.weather.storm/2: A proper storm. My gran said these washed the year's bad luck off the roof. I'll believe it if it lets up.
dialogue.conversations.weather.rain: This rain? The crops love it even if my boots don't. We needed it, honestly.
dialogue.conversations.weather.rain/1: Grey and drizzly. Good sleeping weather, bad laundry weather. I know which I'd rather have.
dialogue.conversations.weather.rain/2: Rain again. The well's happy, the road's mud, and the frogs are showing off. Balance, I suppose.
dialogue.conversations.weather.clear: Not a cloud up there. Days like this you forgive the place its winters.
dialogue.conversations.weather.clear/1: Clear skies and warm sun — I'd get twice the work done if I didn't keep stopping to enjoy it.
dialogue.conversations.weather.clear/2: Good clean sky today. Makes even the cracked bell and the muddy square look almost handsome.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.grieving: Ah. You heard, then. We lost one of our own. The whole village feels the gap. ...Thank you for asking, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.grieving/: It's been a mournful few days here. Someone's chair sits empty. I keep expecting them round the corner.
There's grief in the streets just now. We hold each other up when it comes. Kind of you to notice, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.elated: Oh, it's a good few days! There's been happy news in the village — you can feel it in the square.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.elated/1: Everyone's lighter this week, %1$s. Good things have happened close to home, and the joy spreads.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.elated/2: Can't you feel it? The whole village is grinning about something. I've caught it too, and I'm not fighting it.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.fine: Same as ever, thanks for asking. Ups and downs, mostly evens. That's village life.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.fine/1: Steady enough. No news worth the word, which is its own kind of good, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.fine/2: Oh, plodding along. The bell rings, the bread bakes, I complain, I sleep. Comforting, really.
dialogue.conversations.season.spring: Spring suits me. Everything's waking up — green on the fields, lambs in the pen, mud on every doorstep.
dialogue.conversations.season.spring/1: You can smell the thaw, %1$s. I've seeds to get in the ground and I'll not waste a day of it.
dialogue.conversations.season.spring/2: New season, new start. The birds are back and so's my good mood, near enough.
dialogue.conversations.season.summer: High summer — long days, short tempers by the forge, and cold well-water that's worth its weight in gold.
dialogue.conversations.season.summer/1: Warm enough to work till the light's gone. I'll be glad of the shade come noon, mind.
dialogue.conversations.season.summer/2: The summer's good to us, %1$s. Crops standing tall and the market full. Make the most of it before the turn.
dialogue.conversations.season.autumn: Autumn already. The leaves are going gold and I've the harvest and the woodpile both on my mind.
dialogue.conversations.season.autumn/1: There's a bite in the mornings now. Time to lay stores by before winter comes knocking, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.season.autumn/2: I love the fall, honestly. Everything ripe at once, then the quiet after. Bittersweet, that.
dialogue.conversations.season.winter: Winter's here, and it doesn't ask permission. I keep the fire fed and my complaints to myself. Mostly.
dialogue.conversations.season.winter/1: Cold enough to crack stone, %1$s. Wrap up out there — the road ices over past the well.
dialogue.conversations.season.winter/2: We hunker down this time of year. Stew on the pot, snow on the sill, and a long wait for green.
dialogue.conversations.season.any: Season's turning like it always does. I just keep pace with it and try not to grumble too loud.
dialogue.conversations.season.any/1: Oh, the year rolls on, %1$s. Some days I mark it, most days the work does the marking for me.
dialogue.conversations.season.any/2: Same wheel it always is — sun, rain, harvest, frost. Comforting to know what's coming, I find.
dialogue.conversations.season.holiday.sp: You picked the spring bloom to visit! The whole village is out with flowers in their hair. Even I've got a sprig.
It's the bloom, %1$s — first flowers of the year. We hang garlands and pretend winter never happened.
Spring bloom today! The children have been weaving crowns since dawn. Try one on, you've earned it.
dialogue.conversations.season.holiday.mi: Midsummer! Longest day of the year — there'll be a bonfire in the square tonight, and I'll not miss it.
It's the midsummer feast, %1$s. Dance till the short dark and sleep it off tomorrow. That's the tradition.
Feel that sun? Midsummer's come round again. We light the fires at dusk to keep the light a little longer.
dialogue.conversations.season.holiday.ha: Harvest festival! Barns full, tables fuller. Sit with us tonight, %1$s — nobody eats alone this evening.
It's harvest home. A year's work's in the store at last, and we thank the fields the only way we know — a feast.
Best day of the autumn, this. The harvest's in, the ale's out, and even I'll crack a smile before the night's done.
dialogue.conversations.season.holiday.mi: Midwinter's night — the year's darkest. We light every candle we've got and dare the dark to outlast us.
It's midwinter, %1$s. Cold and long, but the whole village gathers close and shares what little warmth there is.
Deep midwinter. We tell the old stories tonight and toast to the light coming back. It always does, in the end.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.first: Hoping for? A good harvest, a quiet winter, and to see the people I love do well. Simple things, %1$s. The best ones usually are.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.first/1: I try not to hope too loud — but if you're asking, I'd like the roof to hold another year and the little ones to grow up kind.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.first/2: What am I hoping for? That things stay steady. That the ones who left come back. That's enough to be going on with.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.again: You already asked what I'm hoping for, %1$s. My wishes haven't changed since breakfast.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.again/1: Same hopes as before. They don't turn over that quickly, mine.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.again/2: Asking twice won't make them come true any faster. But I appreciate the interest.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.revisit: I've thought more about what I said I was hoping for. There's one wish under all the others I didn't mention.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.revisit/1: Remember I told you my hopes, %1$s? I left the biggest one off the list. Maybe another day I'll say it.
dialogue.conversations.hopes.revisit/2: Been turning my hopes over since you asked. Funny how naming them makes them feel closer to real.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.none: Rumors? It's been dead quiet, %1$s. Not so much as a misplaced goat to talk about.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.none/1: Nothing's going round just now. Give the village a week — there's always something eventually.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.none/2: No fresh talk that I've heard. And I'd have heard it, believe me. These walls are thin.
dialogue.chatmode.confused: Hm? I didn't quite catch that.
dialogue.chatmode.confused/2: I'm not sure what you mean, %1$s.
dialogue.chatmode.topics: my day, my work, the village, or how I've been
dialogue.chatmode.hint/1: Not sure what you're after — maybe ask about %2$s?
dialogue.chatmode.hint/2: We could talk about %2$s, if you like.
dialogue.chatmode.busy: Give me a moment — I'm in the middle of something.
dialogue.chatmode.busy/1: One moment, I'm busy just now.
dialogue.chatmode.busy/2: Can it wait? My hands are full.
dialogue.chatmode.muted/2: As you wish — I'll say no more.
dialogue.chatmode.hail/1: Well met, %1$s. Good to see you about.
dialogue.chatmode.hail/2: Ah, %1$s! I was hoping I'd run into you.
dialogue.chatmode.hail/3: There's a face I don't mind seeing. Hello.
dialogue.chatmode.confused.toddler: Huh? I dunno what that means.
dialogue.chatmode.hint.toddler: I only know little stuff... like %2$s!
dialogue.chatmode.hint.toddler/1: Um, um... you could ask about %2$s?
dialogue.chatmode.shrug.toddler/1: *shrugs so hard they nearly topple over*
dialogue.chatmode.clarify.toddler/1: %2$s? Or %3$s? I forgot which you said.
dialogue.chatmode.dropped.toddler/1: Okay okay. What else, what else?
dialogue.chatmode.busy.toddler/1: Not now — I'm super duper busy.
dialogue.chatmode.muted.toddler: Okay... I'll be quiet now. Shhh.
dialogue.chatmode.insult.toddler: That's a mean word. I'm telling!
dialogue.chatmode.hail_cold.toddler: *peeks out from behind a fence post*
dialogue.chatmode.hail_cold.toddler/1: I'm not s'posed to talk to you.
dialogue.chatmode.kidtopic: I dunno 'bout that. That's grown-up talk.
dialogue.chatmode.kidtopic/1: That sounds like big-people stuff. Wanna see my mud pie instead?
dialogue.conversations.topic.day.rough.r: That's the shape of the day, more or less.
dialogue.conversations.topic.day.ordinar: That's about the size of it.
dialogue.conversations.topic.day.rough.r: That sounds like a lot to carry.
dialogue.conversations.topic.day.rough.f: Let me take something off your hands.
You don't have to make it into anything.
dialogue.conversations.topic.day.rough.r: That came out wrong. I'm sorry.
I'm not going to pretend it's a tragedy.
dialogue.conversations.topic.day.good.re: You've earned a day like that.
What made it a good one?
Must be nice. Some of us work.
Glad to hear it. I'll get on.
dialogue.conversations.topic.day.good.fo: Careful — people will think you're happy.
dialogue.conversations.topic.day.ordinar: Don't let me slow you down, then.
You could do that faster, you know.
I'll stop talking and let you finish.
I'll get out of your way.
dialogue.conversations.topic.day.young.r: That sounds like a good day's work.
I'll let you get back to it.
dialogue.conversations.topic.day.young.f: Is that how it usually goes?
dialogue.conversations.topic.day.toddler: That is the best news I've heard all day.
dialogue.conversations.day.plain: Ordinary. Nothing's broken and nothing's on fire. I'll take ordinary.
dialogue.conversations.day.plain/1: It's a Tuesday sort of day. Even when it isn't.
dialogue.conversations.day.plain/2: Fine. Uneventful. Which around here counts as a small victory.
dialogue.conversations.day.rough.empathi: It is, a bit. Nice of you to notice instead of telling me it could be worse.
Some days are just heavy. Thank you for not trying to fix it in one sentence.
That's all it needed, honestly. Somebody saying it out loud.
dialogue.conversations.day.rough.ask: The short version? Everything that could tip over, tipped over. In order.
dialogue.conversations.day.rough.ask/1: Nothing dramatic. Just a hundred small things, all pulling the same direction.
dialogue.conversations.day.rough.ask/2: It started with the door sticking and got creative from there.
dialogue.conversations.day.rough.brush_o: Suppose they do. Doesn't make this one lighter, but suppose they do.
Mm. That's the sort of thing people say when they'd rather not hear the answer.
dialogue.conversations.day.rough.leave: Go on, then. The day'll keep.
dialogue.conversations.day.rough.leave/2: Fair enough. I'll be here, being tired at things.
dialogue.conversations.day.rough.offer_h: You mean that? ...Alright. That's the first useful thing that's happened today.
Hands, not sympathy. You're a rare one, %1$s.
I'll take you up on that. Don't offer twice unless you mean it.
dialogue.conversations.day.rough.lighten: Ha! The cat won. The cat always wins. Right — I feel better and I resent it.
You're terrible. ...That's the first time I've laughed since the stew hit the floor.
Ha. Alright. Alright. Point to you.
...I'm sure that's funny somewhere. Not in here.
Please don't. Not today. Today I'd rather it just be bad.
Mm. Very clever, %1$s. I'm going to go back to my day now.
Heh. The cat did win, to be fair.
That's about the size of it, yes.
Suppose you have to laugh. Or you'd do the other thing.
dialogue.conversations.day.rough.let_be: ...No. I don't, do I. That's a relief, actually.
dialogue.conversations.day.rough.let_be/: Everyone wants to make it into a lesson. You didn't. Thank you.
It can just be a bad day. Feels strange to be allowed that.
dialogue.conversations.day.rough.apologi: ...Alright. It did come out wrong. We'll leave it there.
Accepted. Don't make a habit of it, %1$s.
Mm. Thank you for saying so. It's more than most manage.
dialogue.conversations.day.rough.double_: No. It's not a tragedy. It's just mine, and you've made it heavier. Good day.
Then keep it to yourself next time. I've plenty to be getting on with.
Right. I'll remember you said that, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.day.good.celebrat: Earned it? I'll take that. Nobody says that around here.
Hah. Don't tell the others, they'll want one.
Maybe I have. Feels good to hear it said, anyway.
dialogue.conversations.day.good.ask_more: Small things. Cold water, short queue, nobody needed anything urgently. That's the recipe.
Nothing went wrong. That's the whole of it. It's rarer than it sounds.
The bread came out right. You can build a whole day on that.
dialogue.conversations.day.good.deflate: ...Right. Well. Sorry for having an hour that didn't hurt.
dialogue.conversations.day.good.deflate/: Everyone works, %1$s. Some of us also have days. Try one.
That's a way to take the shine off a thing.
dialogue.conversations.day.good.leave: Aye, off you go. Enjoy yours if you get one.
dialogue.conversations.day.good.leave/1: Right you are. Good day to you, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.day.good.leave/2: Go on then. Don't let me keep you from the good weather.
dialogue.conversations.day.good.share_ow: Two of us having a good day. The village won't know what to do with itself.
Is that right? Good. It's better when it's going round.
Then we should quit while we're ahead, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.day.good.tease.la: Let them think it! I'll deny it under questioning.
Happy? Slanderous. I'll have you know I'm merely not miserable.
Ha! Don't tell anyone. I've a reputation.
dialogue.conversations.day.good.tease.fl: I am allowed one, you know. It doesn't need commentary.
Mm. And now I'm thinking about it, which rather spoils it.
Must you? It was going so well.
dialogue.conversations.day.good.tease.po: They'd be shocked, I'm sure. Let them be.
One day a season. That's the arrangement.
dialogue.conversations.day.good.wish_wel: So do I. Kind of you to say it out loud.
From your mouth to the weather's ears, %1$s.
It won't, but I appreciate the thought.
dialogue.conversations.day.ordinary.ask_: This? Nothing clever. But it wants doing properly, and that takes as long as it takes.
Same as most days. Which is the point of it, really.
Ask me in an hour and I'll have something to show you.
dialogue.conversations.day.ordinary.shar: Then we're both having the same unremarkable day. Company, of a sort.
Ha. Solidarity in nothing much happening.
Good. Days like this are underrated, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.day.ordinary.hurr: ...You asked. Suppose I'll get back to it, then.
Right. Wouldn't want to waste your time with an answer.
Mm. Next time just walk past, it's quicker for both of us.
dialogue.conversations.day.ordinary.leav: Aye. Mind the puddle by the gate.
Off you go. It'll all still be here.
dialogue.conversations.day.ordinary.prai: ...Well. Not much call for saying so, but I am. Thank you.
Twenty years of it. You'd hope so.
That's landed better than you'd think, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.day.ordinary.advi: Go on then... huh. That would be faster. Right. Noted.
Say that again? ...No, you're right. I've been doing it the long way.
Blunt. Useful. I'll take blunt and useful over polite any day.
Could I. Thank you. I'll add that to the list of things I'm apparently doing wrong.
Mm. I'm sure it looks simple from where you're stood.
Maybe. Maybe there's a reason it's done this way.
Everyone's got a faster way. Mine has the advantage of working.
dialogue.conversations.day.ordinary.let_: Appreciated. Stay if you like — quiet company is fine company.
That's the politest thing anyone's said to me today.
Aye. Talk's easier when the hands are busy anyway.
dialogue.conversations.day.young.interes: Really? Nobody ever wants the long version. Right — so —
You actually want to hear it? Alright!
Hah. Fine. Sit down, this takes a minute.
dialogue.conversations.day.young.encoura: It was, wasn't it! Nobody counts it as work but it IS.
...Huh. Thanks. Most people just say 'that's nice'.
See, that's what I keep saying.
dialogue.conversations.day.young.dismiss: Right. Grown-up news only. Got it.
You asked, though. That's the bit I don't get.
dialogue.conversations.day.young.leave/2: Alright. Come back when you've got more time.
dialogue.conversations.day.young.play_al: AND THEN — right, so — you're the only one who ever lets me finish.
Then it got worse! In the good way!
You're going to regret asking. I've got three more.
dialogue.conversations.day.young.ask_mor: Mostly, yeah. Some days are better. Today was a good one.
Depends on the day. Depends who's about.
More or less. It's alright here, mostly.
dialogue.conversations.day.toddler.delig: It WAS the best! You get it!
dialogue.conversations.day.toddler.ask: Lots. This many. No — THIS many.
dialogue.conversations.day.toddler.ask/1: It was big. Bigger than a duck.
dialogue.conversations.day.toddler.ask/2: I don't remember but it was GOOD.
dialogue.conversations.day.toddler.leave: Okay bye! I'm going to go do it again!
dialogue.conversations.day.again.apologi: Happens. My days blur together too, if I'm honest.
No harm done, %1$s. Ask me tomorrow and I'll have new material.
That's alright. Half of me forgot I answered.
dialogue.conversations.day.again.press: It's the same day, %1$s. It's been the same day for an hour.
dialogue.conversations.day.again.press/1: Asking twice doesn't get you a better answer. It gets you a shorter one.
dialogue.conversations.day.again.press/2: ...Fine. It's fine. It was fine before, too.
dialogue.conversations.day.again.leave/1: Go on. I'll have something new by evening.
dialogue.conversations.topic.fears.press: I've said what I'm going to say.
dialogue.conversations.topic.fears.guard: Some doors stay shut a while.
dialogue.conversations.topic.fears.scarr: You know why it's like this.
dialogue.conversations.arc.fears.followt: You remember what I told you.
Tell me the rest of it.
Thank you for telling me. I'll go.
I can't promise that. But I'm listening.
You could face it, you know.
Thank you for trusting me with that.
dialogue.conversations.topic.fears.guard: Fair enough. It's yours to keep.
dialogue.conversations.topic.fears.scarr: I pushed you, and I was wrong to.
dialogue.conversations.topic.fears.again: Sorry — I shouldn't have asked twice.
dialogue.conversations.topic.fears.toddl: That does sound scary. You're safe here.
What's it like, the scary thing?
dialogue.conversations.topic.fears.young: That's a real thing to be scared of.
Everyone I know is scared of something.
dialogue.conversations.arc.fears.plan.re: Then let's do something about it.
You don't need a plan. I'm here.
dialogue.conversations.arc.fears.followt: Look at you. That's not nothing.
I meant what I said, back then.
I'll not make a fuss of it.
dialogue.conversations.fears.scarred: ...You. Right. Ask me about the weather, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.fears.scarred/1: I remember how the last one went. Let's not.
dialogue.conversations.fears.scarred/2: That door's got a bolt on it now. You put it there.
dialogue.conversations.fears.resume.plan: That thing I told you about. It hasn't gone anywhere.
I've been thinking about what I said to you. Out loud didn't kill me.
It's still sat there, the fear. Politely. Waiting.
dialogue.conversations.fears.resume.foll: I did the thing. Or started it. You'll want to hear.
Small progress on the old fear. Small counts.
Ask me about it. Go on. I've earned the asking.
dialogue.conversations.fears.open.comfor: ...You mean that. You're not just being polite. Then here's the part I never say: it isn't the thing itself. It's that I'd be alone in it.
Careful, %1$s. Kindness like that makes a person put the whole thing down. ...There. It's down.
...Thank you. Most people change the subject.
You didn't laugh. That's rarer than you'd think.
Mm. It is. Not much to be done about it, though.
Kind of you. It doesn't move, but it's kind.
Don't. I didn't hand you that so you could pat it on the head.
Soft words, %1$s? It isn't a soft thing. Leave it be.
That's... yes. It is hard to carry. Thank you for saying so.
Most people go quiet when I say it. You didn't.
Heavy's the word for it, aye.
...You don't flinch, do you. Alright. The rest of it, the true shape — and it stays between us.
Persistent. And gentle about it, which is worse. ...Fine. All of it, then.
There's more, yes. Give me a breath. ...There. Two of us carrying it now.
You pull gently, I'll give you that. A little more of it, then.
Some of it, maybe. Not tonight. Tonight's too much like the night it happened.
That thread's still attached to something. Later. I mean later, not never.
I said what I said. The rest is mine. Leave it.
No. Some doors you don't knock on twice in a day, %1$s.
There's more to it. Whether you get it is another question.
Bold, asking for the rest. Give me a moment with that.
Mm. Not sure I've decided how much of it you get.
dialogue.conversations.fears.open.share: You too? Huh. It's less heavy when two people carry it.
dialogue.conversations.fears.open.share/: Strange comfort, that. Two cowards make one brave pair.
Then we watch each other's backs. That's how it's meant to work.
dialogue.conversations.fears.open.leave: Aye. Thank you for not making a thing of it.
dialogue.conversations.fears.open.leave/: Go on. It'll keep until next time, %1$s.
Right. Well. That's enough honesty for one afternoon.
dialogue.conversations.fears.open.pledge: ...Nobody's said that before. I'm holding you to it, %1$s.
Not alone. Right. I'll try to believe that.
Careful what you promise. I remember promises.
dialogue.conversations.fears.open.step_b: ...That's honest. I'd rather that than a promise you'd break.
Good. People promise too easily around here. Listening is enough.
No promises. Understood. You still stayed, though.
dialogue.conversations.fears.open.challe: ...Nobody ever offered the 'with you' part before. That's the part that matters. Alright. Next storm, I'll stand in the doorway.
You'd actually stand there with me. Huh. Fine. I'm holding you to it, and you're holding me to it.
Maybe. With a witness, maybe. Don't let me back out of it later.
You make it sound almost possible. Ask me again when it's close.
Easy for you — you've somewhere else to be when it goes wrong.
Hm. Half of me believes you. The other half keeps the accounts.
Don't make my fear a test of your character. It isn't yours to be brave about.
Face it, you say. You'll be gone by frost like everyone else.
Maybe I could. Not today, but maybe.
That's a thought I'll be carrying around now. Thanks for that.
You say it like it's simple. It might even be.
dialogue.conversations.fears.open.thank: You don't have to thank me for it. ...But thank you for the thanking.
dialogue.conversations.fears.open.thank/: It's not a gift, %1$s. It's just true. Still — aye. You're welcome.
Trust's a strange thing to be thanked for. I'll take it.
dialogue.conversations.fears.open.means: ...It did. More than I'd like to admit standing here.
dialogue.conversations.fears.open.means/: Saying it out loud was the hard part. You made it easier.
Noticed that, did you. Most don't.
dialogue.conversations.fears.open.close_: Aye. Go on. And %1$s — thank you.
Right. Enough of that. Mind how you go.
Off with you. We'll pretend this was about the weather.
dialogue.conversations.fears.pressed.bac: ...Thank you. Not many people can stop when they're told to.
That's the right answer, %1$s. I'll remember you gave it.
Good. The rest will come when it comes, or it won't.
dialogue.conversations.fears.pressed.pus: No. NO. You were told, and you asked again. Get away from me.
That's what you are, then. Someone who takes. I won't forget it, %1$s.
You cracked it open because you wanted to see. I hope it was worth the look.
dialogue.conversations.fears.pressed.lea: Go on, then. Before either of us says more.
dialogue.conversations.fears.guarded.res: ...Aye. It is mine. Thank you for hearing that the first time.
Most people push. You didn't. That buys you something, %1$s.
Good. Ask me again in a season and we'll see.
dialogue.conversations.fears.guarded.ask: Now that I can do. Ask me about the crops, or the roof, or the cat.
Something easier. Aye. Let's start there and work up.
Sensible. Small talk first, %1$s. That's how it's built.
dialogue.conversations.fears.guarded.pre: I said no. Do you want to hear it a second time?
You'll be wanting my savings next. It's a no, %1$s.
Pushing at a locked door only tells me about you.
dialogue.conversations.fears.guarded.lea: Off you go. No hard feelings.
Right you are. We'll get there or we won't.
dialogue.conversations.fears.scarred.apo: ...Took you long enough. It doesn't undo it. But it's something.
You were wrong, aye. Saying so out loud costs you something, so — noted.
I'll not pretend it never happened, %1$s. But you can stand there.
dialogue.conversations.fears.scarred.giv: Good. That's the only thing left that helps.
Aye. Space. I'd rather that than another apology.
Right. Then we'll both get on with our days.
dialogue.conversations.fears.again.apolo: It's alright. It's not the sort of thing that gets easier by repetition.
No harm. Ask me in a few days and I'll have found new words.
Appreciated, %1$s. Twice in a day is a lot to ask of anyone.
dialogue.conversations.fears.again.press: I already showed you that scar. Don't poke it twice in one week.
Twice? Buy me a drink first, %1$s.
Let it rest. It bites when it's poked fresh.
dialogue.conversations.fears.again.leave: Right. Catch me when the week's turned.
Good. Some things want a gap between them.
dialogue.conversations.fears.toddler.rea: You'd tell me if there WAS a monster though. Promise?
Okay. I feel a bit braver now.
dialogue.conversations.fears.toddler.ask: It's big. And it doesn't have a face. THAT'S the bad part.
It lives under there. Only at night. It's very rude.
I don't want to say it out loud. It might hear.
dialogue.conversations.fears.young.reass: ...Yeah. It is. Everyone acts like it's stupid.
Thanks. Most grown-ups just say 'don't be silly'.
dialogue.conversations.fears.young.norma: Everyone? Even you? ...Huh. That helps, actually.
So it's not just me being weird about it. Good.
Everyone's scared of something. I'll hold onto that.
dialogue.conversations.fears.young.dismi: Grow out of it. Sure. That's what people say when they've stopped listening.
dialogue.conversations.fears.young.leave: Alright. Don't tell anyone I said that.
dialogue.conversations.fears.plan.ask_wh: You remember all of it, don't you. Even the part I nearly didn't say. ...Company. That's what helps.
Most people forget by the next morning. You didn't. Not being alone with it — that's the answer.
Since you actually listened the first time: someone knowing. That's most of it, %1$s.
Honestly? I don't know. Nobody's asked me that before.
What would help. Huh. Give me a moment with that one.
Not being talked out of it, for a start.
dialogue.conversations.fears.plan.offer_: Do something about it. You make it sound like a chore list. ...Maybe it is.
Alright. Something small, then. I'm not promising heroics.
A plan. Nobody's ever given the thing a plan before, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.fears.plan.just_l: ...No plan. Just this. That's better than a plan, actually.
Everyone wants to fix it. You just stood there. Thank you.
Being here is the whole of it, some days.
dialogue.conversations.fears.plan.leave: Aye. It'll wait. It's good at waiting.
dialogue.conversations.fears.plan.leave/: Go on. We'll pick it up.
Right. Thank you for coming back to it at all.
dialogue.conversations.fears.followthrou: Slowly. But slowly is a direction, which is more than I had.
Two bad nights, one fine one. I'll take the arithmetic.
Better than it was. Ask me again next week and we'll see if I'm lying.
...It isn't nothing, is it. I keep telling myself it's nothing.
Don't make me proud of it, I'll get insufferable.
Someone noticing is half of why it worked, %1$s.
You did say that. And you turned up, which is the rarer half of a promise.
I know. I've been keeping the receipt, %1$s. You're square with me.
Not alone, you said. It turns out that was the useful bit.
You didn't promise anything. I remember. That's why I believed the rest of it.
You were honest instead of kind. It wore better than kind would have.
No promises from you, %1$s. And here you are anyway, asking.
Aye. Best not to stare at it too long.
Right. Off you go. It's still there, but it's smaller.
Go on. And thank you for keeping track.
